title: Local storage and privacy
description: Understand what Quickque stores on a device, what remains temporary, and where local-network and screen-sharing boundaries matter.
body:
# Local storage and privacy

Quickque is designed to keep a personal meeting script close to the device. There is no Quickque account, cloud script library, cloud transcription service, analytics pipeline, or silent online fallback in the current app. Local-first is a boundary to understand, not a promise that every device or network is automatically safe.

## Temporary dummy checkout

Quickque source and documentation remain available under the [MIT License](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/LICENSE). The planned app is free to use with 30 seconds of Voice Follow per session. Unlimited Voice Follow and saved AI rehearsal audio are planned at £2.50/month or £25 for a lifetime licence. Payments and paid activation are not implemented yet. The native Free session timer is implemented and awaiting Mac verification.

Payment-provider processing is disabled. The temporary dummy checkout runs only in the browser, collects no card, billing, contact, or payment details, charges no money, and creates no order, licence, entitlement, or download. The website backend does not create or verify payment sessions. See the [dummy commerce runbook](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/artifacts/quickque-website/docs/COMMERCE.md) for the current boundary.

## Before you begin

- Decide which browser origin or desktop app you intend to use; their storage is separate.
- Back up scripts before clearing site data, uninstalling, moving scripts to Trash, permanently deleting them, or moving between the browser and Mac app.
- Use the native app only on a Mac and network you trust. Review the [Phone Remote](/guide/phone-remote/) warning about unencrypted local HTTP.

## What persists locally

1. The library envelope in local device storage includes live scripts, the active selection, Trash entries, custom order, and sort mode. Library state is committed together so a failed write does not claim a partial save.

2. Reader and appearance settings such as Dark Theme, Overlay Opacity, font size, scroll speed, and Compact Overlay preference are stored separately from the library backup.

3. A successful Flow model installation is durably cached under `~/Library/Application Support/Quickque/Flow/` on the Mac. Model files are not included in Export script backup.

4. Use Settings → Export script backup when you need a portable copy. The JSON contains scripts, active selection, Trash, custom order, and sort mode, but not settings or Flow models. See [Backup, restore, and migration](/guide/backup-restore/).

## Saved AI rehearsal audio

The paid Mac audio feature generates Chatterbox dialogue locally and saves WAV audio under the app’s application-support folder, associated with the script identity. Performance edits prepare AI Partner lines; presentation narration is optional and starts only with Generate audio. Notes and In Person lines are not generated. These files persist after playback and app restart. JSON backups do not include generated audio. Use Remove saved audio in Edit to remove a script’s cache, ideally before permanently deleting the script. Export MP4 writes a separate audio file to the destination you choose. Licence activation and Mac verification are still outstanding.

## What remains temporary

1. Local Flow captures the selected microphone, never system audio, and processes it in memory. Audio is not written to a recording or sent to a service.

2. Recognition events and transcript text are transient. Quickque does not save, back up, or log transcripts.

3. Document import reads selected bytes in a disposable bundled worker. It makes no upload, executes no document markup, renders no imported HTML, and fetches no embedded resources. Review text becomes persistent only when you choose Save as Script.

4. Phone Remote exchanges minimal reader state and validated control commands over the local session. It does not serve script text, audio, transcripts, model files, or library contents. Its local HTTP transport is unencrypted.

## Safer use

1. Export a full backup before changing storage, deleting a script, or uninstalling the app. Store it privately because it contains script text.

2. Grant microphone permission only when you intentionally choose Start microphone in native Flow.

3. Pair Phone Remote only on a trusted reachable LAN, approve the expected phone on the Mac, and stop the session when finished.

4. Choose only the intended application or window when sharing Zoom or Meet. The Mac overlay can appear in screen sharing or recording.

5. When moving between browser and desktop, export from the source and import in the destination. Existing web storage is not migrated automatically.

## Expected result

Scripts, Trash, ordering, settings, and deliberately installed models stay on their respective local origins or Mac storage. Microphone audio and recognition text disappear from Quickque working memory when Flow stops. Generated rehearsal audio and exported MP4 files persist until removed. The dummy checkout transmits no payment information because it makes no payment request.

## Troubleshooting

- **My browser and desktop have different scripts:** separate localStorage origins are expected. Use Export script backup and Import script backup.
- **A transcript appears after Flow stops:** Quickque does not persist transcript events as a recording, backup, or transcript log. Report any reproducible persisted file.
- **Phone Remote feels private because it is local:** local does not mean encrypted. Use a trusted LAN only.
- **A document import seems to need the internet:** it should not fetch document resources or a runtime CDN. Stop and investigate the request.
- **The dummy checkout asks for payment details:** stop immediately. The current demo must never request them or leave the Quickque website.
- **Screen sharing shows Quickque:** share a specific meeting window instead of the whole display.

Privacy-sensitive behavior, microphone permission, native packaging, and physical remote behavior still need Mac verification. Read [Requirements and installation](/guide/requirements-installation/) for the current release status.
